body:
In [my initial PR](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/pull/5952/changes), I did it like this: `const agent = new ProxyAgent()`, **without** passing a proxy value, and without ternary syntax: `ProxyAgent` lib handle it all automatically.

That’s the [recommended way to initialize the proxy-agent library](https://github.com/TooTallNate/proxy-agents/tree/main/packages/proxy-agent#example), because:

* there are different kinds of proxies (HTTPS, PAC, SOCKS, etc.)
* it automatically respects the `no_proxy` environment variable, so some URLs can bypass the proxy

There are a few other reasons I [mentioned earlier](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/pull/5952):

* it works if `HTTPS_PROXY` (uppercase) is set instead of `https_proxy`
* it supports `http_proxy` (not HTTPS), for cases like using an HTTP `REGISTRY_URL`
* it allows dynamic proxy settings (PAC files)

You also said you tested it manually with `https_proxy=http://<proxy>:<port>`, which is good. But the other cases I mentioned weren’t tested (no offense, I know proxy testing is quite painful to be honest). My proposed code here also handled `no_proxy`, and I verified that behavior in the initial PR.

Thanks @pomeh — you were right that proxy support was thin, and I'd missed this in the first round of the PR.

One small correction on the API: `new ProxyAgent()` (no argument) works for the [`proxy-agent`](https://github.com/TooTallNate/proxy-agents/tree/main/packages/proxy-agent) package you used in #5952, but **undici's `ProxyAgent` is a different class** despite the identical name. From [undici's typings](https://github.com/nodejs/undici/blob/main/types/proxy-agent.d.ts):

```ts
constructor (options: ProxyAgent.Options | string)
```

The `uri` is required — no-arg construction throws.

For the env-var-aware behavior you described, undici ships a separate class: **`EnvHttpProxyAgent`**. I've switched to it in 2784955d9, which now honors:

- `HTTPS_PROXY` / `https_proxy`
- `HTTP_PROXY` / `http_proxy`
- `NO_PROXY` / `no_proxy`

Coverage is locked in by:

- **Unit tests** for the env-detection factory (`packages/shadcn/src/registry/proxy.test.ts`)
- **Integration test** that spins up a real CONNECT-tunneling HTTP proxy and verifies routing + `NO_PROXY` bypass end-to-end (`packages/shadcn/src/registry/proxy.integration.test.ts`)

PAC files and SOCKS proxies aren't supported by `EnvHttpProxyAgent`, but they weren't supported by the previous `https-proxy-agent` setup either — those would require bringing back the broader `proxy-agent` package, which conflicts with this PR's goal of dropping unmaintained transitive deps. Happy to follow up in a separate PR if there's appetite.

Thanks again for catching this.

Update on this thread: I went further than my initial reply scoped — partly because the framing in your original review (this is the natural opportunity to fix the broader proxy gaps, not just the env-var detection) was the right one.

The PR now supports:

| Capability | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `HTTPS_PROXY` / `https_proxy` | partial | ✅ |
| `HTTP_PROXY` / `http_proxy` | ❌ | ✅ |
| `NO_PROXY` / `no_proxy` bypass | ❌ | ✅ |
| `ALL_PROXY=socks*://...` (SOCKS4/5) | ❌ | ✅ |
| `PAC_URL=...` (PROXY/SOCKS/DIRECT routing) | ❌ | ✅ |

I was wrong in my earlier reply that adding SOCKS/PAC would require bringing back `proxy-agent` — there's a cleaner path that doesn't reintroduce the abandoned-deps concern:

- **SOCKS** via [`socks`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/socks): plugs directly into undici's dispatcher model via a custom undici `Agent` with a `socks`-based `connect` factory. ~50KB, actively maintained, zero runtime deps.
- **PAC** via [`pac-resolver`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/pac-resolver) + [`quickjs-wasi`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/quickjs-wasi): the JS engine is exposed independently of any HTTP-Agent adapter, so we evaluate PAC and route the result through our own dispatcher selection (HTTP / SOCKS / DIRECT).

PAC support pulls in `quickjs-wasi` (~3 MB WASM blob) for sandboxed PAC script execution. Material for a CLI install but accepted deliberately — PAC scripts can come from network-supplied WPAD discovery where execution isolation matters.

Coverage: **23 unit tests + 13 integration tests** (36 total). Integration tests run a real local CONNECT-tunneling HTTP proxy, a hand-rolled SOCKS5 server, and a local PAC file server — verifying end-to-end routing for each mechanism plus per-host PAC directives.

Title and description on this PR have been updated to reflect the broader scope. Thanks again for the original push.

I see 2 strange things here:

1. proxy should not alter the payload from request or response. The origin server responds with `{ from: "origin" }` while proxy server respond with `{ from: "proxy-direct" }`, which are 2 distinct body values. Whether you use a proxy or not, the payload should be the same.
2. I see no other occurrence of value `proxy-direct` elsewhere in this test code. This means the `proxy-direct` is never checked for, which, I guess, can mean several things:
    1. the proxy is never called, thus never return `proxy-direct` JSON value
    2. the proxy is called, but its JSON payload body is totally ignored (and `from: "origin"` would be the only response payload we got in all test cases)
    3. the proxy is called, the `proxy-direct` JSON value is returned, but we never test this value explicitly



To avoid the body alteration problem, and also solve the second point, I would propose:

to not alter the response body payload by the proxy
to add a custom, fake, response header by the proxy, such as `X-E2E-Proxy: e2e-proxy-server`

What make me unsure with this is the fact that `proxyHits` is checked, and it effectively contains the value expected when tunneling through the proxy, meaning the test are working normally. In any case, having `proxy-direct` value here and not elsewhere is somewhat disturbing.

why not perform the exact same test as previously ?

```
      // Proof the proxy was used: a CONNECT was recorded against the origin.
      const originHost = new URL(originUrl).host
      expect(proxyHits).toEqual([{ url: originHost, method: "CONNECT" }])
```

Thanks for these update @nbouvrette , looks like to have full proxy support now, including automated tests, which is nice to ensure things are working as expected. What a great work !

I've done 2 smalls remarks on the updated code (regarding tests).

Good catch — the inconsistency was unintentional. Tightened in aeaa78b31 to match the parallel test:

```ts
const originHost = new URL(originUrl).host
expect(proxyHits).toEqual([{ url: originHost, method: "CONNECT" }])
```

The looser version (`.toHaveLength(1)` + `.toBe("CONNECT")`) would have missed bugs where the dispatcher CONNECTed to the wrong host (e.g., the proxy's own address instead of the origin's). The strict version catches that bug class.
